newsitem.title: DENMARK: Goldman rates Carlsberg as underperformer.
newsitem.headline: Goldman rates Carlsberg as underperformer.

text.p: U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs rated Danish brewery group Carlsberg A/S an underperformer in its latest Denmark Research analysis received by Reuters on Friday.

It said that although its products were available in over 150 countries globally, Carlsberg, was heavily exposed in Denmark and the U.K., where 60 percent of its operating profits were generated in 1995.
"These two markets are difficult, with Carlsberg's volumes and prices under pressure at home," Goldman Sachs said in its report.
"In its key foreign market (Britain), Carlsberg faces uncertainty as its merger with Bass awaits regulatory approval," Goldman Sachs said.
In August Carlsberg and Bass agreed that the Danish brewer would hold a 20 percent stake in a merged Carlsberg-Tetley-Bass if British regulators allowed the deal.
Goldman saw Carlsberg 1996 results as flat or declining in every foreign market but Britain, Malawi, Portugal and Malaysia.
It noted that the brewer's extensive use of licensees limited its group requirements, often placing responsibility for its brands in the hands of inadequate operators.
Despite the Goldman Sachs analysis, the Carlsberg share climbed five crowns to 365 by 1130 gmt.
